title: PowerShell Script Block Combining Base64 Decoding With Dynamic Execution
detection_hypothesis: If an obfuscated stage is executed in memory, the logged script block will contain both a base64 decoding call and a dynamic evaluation construct.

field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.
expected_volume: Low; each match usually merits inspection of the decoded content.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches come from a small number of internal modules with stable script paths and predictable schedules. Tune on the Path field and require review before adding any exclusion.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the specific internal module path. Never exclude the decoding call alone, because it is the most reusable part of the pattern.
test_strategy: Positive cases pair decoding with expression invocation and with script block creation. Negative cases use decoding for a file write and evaluation of a literal string.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1027, T1140.
